title: Alien Dictionary
keyIdea: Neighbouring words give the rules: the first letter where they differ says which comes first. Those rules are edges between letters, and a topological sort of that graph is the alphabet. Two ways to fail: a word placed before its own prefix ("abc" then "ab"), or a cycle in the rules.

approaches.name: DFS post-order (3 states)
approaches.idea: Same rules. DFS each letter; add it to out after all the letters it must precede are finished, then reverse out. Meeting a letter still on the current path (state 1) is a cycle → "".
approaches.why: C = total characters in all words: each is read once to collect letters and once while comparing neighbours. The letter graph has at most 26 nodes and 26² edges, so the DFS is a constant amount of work; the recursion is at most 26 deep.

approaches.name: Kahn's algorithm (BFS on indegrees)
approaches.idea: Compare each word with the next: the first differing letters give one rule u → v (indegree[v]++). A longer word before its own prefix → "". Then queue letters with indegree 0, append each one taken, lower its followers' indegrees. If some letters were never taken, they are in a cycle → "".
approaches.why: C = total characters in all words, read a constant number of times. The graph is at most 26 letters with a 26 × 26 table, so Kahn's part is constant work and the extra space is fixed (26² booleans, 26 indegrees).

quiz.q: Words "wrt" then "wrf". What rule do you get?
Why compare only neighbouring words, not every pair?
options: If each neighbour pair is in order, the whole list is; other pairs add no new rules beyond what the sort implies
It is required by the queue
"": a word can never come before its own prefix
Any order of a, b, c

quiz.q: After Kahn's algorithm, 3 letters are in the order but 5 letters appear in the words. What happened?
options: The other 2 are in a cycle, so return ""
They had no rules, so add them at the end

quiz.q: A letter appears in the words but in no rule. Where does it go?
options: Anywhere: it starts with indegree 0 and still must be in the answer
